Macro overlay — from their posts, not our data
A risk-off tape after mega-cap earnings, and the group's split is dip-buyers versus waiters. Prof supplied the chaos read: KOSPI tanking, semis dumping, oil up, mega caps disappointing, and after hours “Sriracha Red” — plus the Binance hack headline (over $5.6 billion stolen, his figure). Venu supplied the broadening: it is no longer just semiconductors, the market is bringing down software stocks too, and the four-year dip-buying playbook is being tested. Enrich ran the busiest board again: a 10/30 watchlist (upside TSLA, RKLB, COST, AAPL; downside NVDA), RKLB's $59 target delivered with contracts paying 70% and 150%, Nasdaq futures tanking overnight, and a longer-horizon note to buy quality companies at a discount over the next few days/weeks. DiCarlo supplied the dip-buys: GOOGL shares bought in the morning of a 12.64% down day, AMZN shares bought despite the earnings drop, BTC back at his Daily Smart Money Zone with $75k as the floor, and INTC's long-term buy ranges finally in reach on what he calls a 16% earnings drop (his figure, not the regular close). Remz supplied the two non-rows: an unnamed huge tech name into major support that could set up a crazy Friday trade if it breaks, and SNDK as unplayable for six months post-split. Sean and iain posted no ticker calls — Sean's system series and iain's process posts (a 50%-drawdown-is-not-a-discount note, a 9-setups cheat sheet, and the empty-pond warning) carry no names. Your process sides with the waiters: no clean qualifier fires today — the nearest live levels are NVDA's downside PDL 0.74% away, META's 30-week reclaim 0.46% away (a repair, not an entry), and BTC's $75k floor; everything else is a completed target (RKLB $59), a broken level (GOOGL $288), a hold at the highs (AAPL, COST, TSLA), or a watch with no stated level (INTC).

More from the group

From the group

Sean — no ticker calls, only the system series: “Over the last two days you've learned my entire system: 1. How to identify the best sectors in the market, 2. Finding the leading stocks in the market, 3. Identifying A+ setups, 4. How to enter these setups, 5. The exit strategy that keeps you in these stocks. Tonight is the…” — quoted to the visible cutoff; plus “Unprofitable traders look for a reason to take a trade every day. Profitable traders look for a reason to sit on their hands until their A+ setup is right in front of them.” No ticker, no level — so Sean has no row today.

iain — process posts, no tickers: “It’s 11:35pm and instead of sleeping, I’m having a theological crisis over why some of y’all keep confusing a 50% drawdown with a 50% discount. Some people will buy a stock down -50% because it’s ‘cheap,’ watch it get smoked another -20% after earnings, then wonder what went…” (quoted to the visible cutoff); “If my commentary has helped even 1 person avoid giving back months of progress these last few weeks, I'm a happy camper”; a 9-setups cheat sheet (“After 5+ years and studying 1000s of charts, I've finally narrowed my entire trading playbook down to these 9 setups”); and “You gotta stop fishing in an empty pond. If the pond is full of life & visible fish, I'm putting my line in the water.”

Remz — the unnamed Friday setup: “There’s one HUGE tech name that’s coming into major support now. If it breaks down tomorrow it can set up for a crazy Friday trade.” No name and no level are given, so no row can follow — it is flagged here rather than guessed at. Plus his 2021–22 dip-buying cautionary tale and a Trump/midterms headline post; his SNDK split call is a row above.

Prof — chaos, red after-hours, and the hack: “Market After hours: Sriracha Red”; “Binance getting absolutely wrecked was NOT on my 2026 bingo card”; “If you own great companies and nothing has changed about why you bought them, sometimes the best thing you can do is delete your brokerage app for a month.” His chaos list and hack headline are in the SPY/QQQ panels and the BTC panel respectively.

Venu — broadening selloff, plus O'Neil: “The market has rewarded dip buyers over the past four years, but remember, we’ve also been in a strong bull market. What worked during a…” (quoted to the visible cutoff); and “One of the most important lessons from William O’Neil’s How to Make Money in Stocks: You don’t need to be right all the time to succeed in the stock market. Even if you’re right only 33% of the time, you can still come out ahead if your winners are significantly bigger than…” (quoted to the visible cutoff).

Enrich — beyond the watchlist: “Please use these next few days / weeks to buy quality companies at a discount. You will be eternally grateful that you did in months / years to come. There are better days ahead, power through”; “Nasdaq futures are absolutely tanking right now”; and a rebranding reaction post with no ticker. His watchlist names are rows above.

DiCarlo — levels live in videos, not posts: all three of his window posts point to videos or breakdowns: the GOOGL setup breakdown, the AMZN breakdown, and the INTC earnings/buy-level post. Where a level is not in the visible post, this feed quotes none rather than guessing from a video title — except $75k for BTC, which is stated in the post itself.

Sources & Methodology
  • Accounts scanned (7): Sean trades @SRxTrades · iain @ohiain · Enrich Trades @enrichtrades · Remz @Remzztrades · Prof @TheProfInvestor · Venu @Venu_7_ · Peter DiCarlo @pdicarlotrader. All seven profiles were readable this window (top ~5 posts visible per account before the login wall). Sean and iain posted no ticker call in this window, so neither has a row — readability is not the constraint, content is.
  • Posts window: Thu Oct 29 – Fri Oct 30, 2026 — everything visible after the Oct 29 feed's window (which ended Oct 29, ~11:45 UTC). Logged-out X shows only the ~5 most recent posts per account; posts truncated in the extraction itself (Sean's system post, iain's drawdown post, Venu's dip-buyer post and O'Neil post, Prof's hack post) are quoted only to the visible cutoff. Where a post is truncated, the feed says so instead of guessing the rest.
  • Price data: Yahoo Finance daily data, as of the Thu Oct 29, 2026 close — this run is pre-market Friday, so Thursday's close is the latest completed close and Friday's session is not in any number here. Moves described as “after hours” (Prof's “Sriracha Red” market note) carry no price and are reported as the trader's words only; every distance-to-trigger in this feed uses the regular close. Trader-stated = a level or call from their post, attributed by name. Chart check = computed by us from that data — it can confirm or push back on a trader's framing, and it's labeled every time. Figure check on INTC: DiCarlo's “down 16%” is his post's figure; the Yahoo regular close is −3.62%, so the 16% reads as the after-hours earnings reaction and is quoted as his words, not adopted as a price.
  • Sector lines: each card's sector/industry ETF comparison (Yahoo Finance, Thu Oct 29, 2026 close) — close, day change, Weinstein stage by the same 30-week MA method, and price vs the 50-week EMA. Mappings: AAPL→XLK, MSFT→IGV, NVDA/INTC/SNDK→SMH, GOOGL/META→XLC, AMZN/TSLA→XLY, RKLB→UFO (space — best fit), COST→XLP (consumer staples — best fit), BTC→IBIT (spot bitcoin). Best-fit choices are noted here, not hidden.
  • Where none of the seven commented on an index, the section says Unavailable / no trader signal — never “unchanged.” IWM and TLT are unavailable this window: no trader mentioned small caps, bonds or rates. SPY and QQQ carry tone labels (not levels): no trader posted an index-specific level or trade call, but Prof's chaos post, Venu's broadening note and Enrich's futures comment are directional market commentary, so the strip synthesizes them as tone and the panels say so.
  • Qualifier rules (constructive pullback into a key MA/support, tightening base near highs, confirmed breakout; never extended/chased). No clean qualifier fires today: the nearest live levels are NVDA's downside PDL (0.74% away, a downside trade not a long qualifier), META's 30-week reclaim (0.46% away, a repair not an entry), and BTC's $75k zone floor (a trader-stated zone buy, held as a watch until the 50-week EMA reclaims). Completed target: RKLB ($59 gap fill delivered). Broken level: GOOGL ($288 gap fill failed, now below the 50-week EMA). Constructive holds, not entries: AAPL (new high), COST, TSLA ($400 hold). Thesis watches, no level: INTC (buy ranges in video). Avoid: SNDK (post-split, Remz). Chart checks only: MSFT, META.
  • Coverage note: nothing is carried over silently. Yesterday's ideas appear here only where today's posts repeat them (TSLA, RKLB from Enrich; GOOGL, AMZN via DiCarlo) — and then only under today's calls, which sometimes differ from yesterday's (RKLB's $59 target is now hit, not pending; GOOGL's $288 level is now broken, not approaching; MSFT's +4.1% after-hours ramp has faded). SKHY, PLTR, MSTR, NBIS, SHOP, VRT, HIMS, ENPH, LITE and the rest of yesterday's board are not rows because today's posts do not repeat those calls.
  • Badge key: Setup describes structure only (green = constructive, amber = pending confirmation, red = broken/extended/avoid). Coverage counts the traders behind a name and is always gray — “Chart only” means no trader mentioned it and implies nothing about the setup. The stage pill next to each ticker (30-week MA basis) is the only place a stage label appears; it is kept out of the prose and the setup badges, and traders' own quoted words are exempt.
  • Level strength: Strong = 2+ confluent anchors (52w high/low, 3m swing, 50-day EMA, 30-week MA, 50-week EMA, trader-stated) within 0.75%, or a 52w extreme with 3+ weekly touches in the past year. Moderate = 1 anchor or 2–3 touches. Light = anything else. Touches count weeks whose high or low came within 0.75% of the level. Duplicate prices merge into one row carrying both labels.
  • Trader charts: none embedded this edition. No trader posted a retrievable chart for a covered name in the visible posts this window, so no trader chart is embedded rather than risking a wrong one.
  • Chart verification gate: every plotted line's endpoint was checked against levels.json before the HTML was built — all 48 computable lines passed within 0.5%. The 30-week MA is a true trailing mean over full 30-week windows only.
